note: Issue 400, institutional-contacts.md section 3 'Gold, for charity'. Placeholder prose: the Author writes the real lines. He writes when his town lives badly, whatever the cause, and asks a sum for its poor. Agreeing is a promise of gold to the TOWN (town-economy.md section 4): when the Crown pays, the town's purse holds it; while the Crown refuses payments the promise breaks and the town receives nothing. No figure in the prose but the sum he asks, which the trigger supplies.

body.text: The people of {param:town} are {perception:people}, and I do not think it will mend of itself.
I am asking {param:amount} for the poor of this parish: blankets, bread, and the rent of families who will otherwise be on the road before the spring.
It is to go to the town, not to me. I should not know what to do with a purse, and the people who would are the reason I am asking.
I know what the Crown is asked for, and by whom. I would only say that this is the one request in the pile that will be spent entirely on people who cannot write to you.

tone.text: {sender:name} — as to the poor of {param:town}, I write {choice}.

options.label: the Crown will pay it
options.text: The Crown will send it, to the town and for the purpose you name.

options.label: the Crown cannot spare it
options.text: The Crown cannot spare it this year. I am sorry for it, and I know that is worth very little to a family on the road.
